title: Spark authorizes a confidentiality exception to its own transparency, letting the Foundation build unannounced deployments
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.10 establishes a framework whose whole purpose is to permit undisclosed activity inside a governance system built on published provisions. A.6.1.1.1.3.10.3 grants Designated Contributors authority to take "any actions reasonably necessary to facilitate the deployment, configuration, testing, maintenance, and operational readiness" of a confidential integration — explicitly including "deployment and configuration of smart contracts, establishment of multisigs or administrative control systems, deployment and configuration of Spark Savings or Morpho vault infrastructure, operation of relayer or frontend infrastructure." Such deployments "may remain undisclosed while applicable confidentiality obligations remain in effect."

The Designated Contributor list (A.6.1.1.1.3.10.2) is one entity: "Spark Foundation may perform actions under this... framework, directly or through contractors or service providers authorized to act on its behalf."

The commercial necessity is real. A distribution partner — an exchange, a fintech, a chain — will not let its integration be announced in a public forum months before launch, and a partner's NDA is not something a DAO can vote away. Spark's alternative to this framework is not more transparency; it is losing the partnerships. The Robinhood Chain and X Layer savings vaults elsewhere in this Artifact are what these arrangements look like once disclosed.

What makes the exception a framework rather than a loophole is that it is itself a published Core provision. The *existence* of confidential activity, the entity permitted to conduct it, the actions permitted, the capital that may not be touched, the liability ceiling, the insurance position, the review requirement and the disclosure deadline are all on the record. Only the specific deal is hidden.

That is the honest way to handle a genuine conflict between openness and commercial reality: bound the secret rather than deny it exists, and publish the bounds.
description: Designated Contributors may deploy contracts, establish multisigs, configure Spark Savings and Morpho vaults and run relayers and frontends while confidentiality obligations remain in effect.
